bihar_raw_news.title: 'Nitish Setu' conceptualised in 2012, named with consensus in honour of JD(U) chief
bihar_raw_news.content: 'Nitish Setu' conceptualised in 2012, named with consensus in honour of JD(U) chief: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary ANI | Updated: Nov 15, 2026 14:42 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna ( Bihar ) [India], November 15 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Sunday asserted that the infrastructure project 'Nitish Setu' is deeply tied to the vision and legacy of former Chief Minister and JD(U) leader Nitish Kumar. "It was conceptualised by Nitish Kumar in 2012. DPR started being prepared in 2012 itself and before the 2015 elections, its foundation stone was laid. So, with a consensus, this has been named as such in his honour," he said. Earlier, Choudhary announced that the 19.76-kilometre-long six-lane corridor connecting Patna and Vaishali districts, scheduled to be inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on November 21, would be named in honour of the JD(U) chief. Meanwhile, Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) MP Manoj Kumar Jha raised questions regarding the timing and political haste of such honours, highlighting that trains have been named after a living person. He also pointed out that the relationship Nitish Kumar shares with Lalu Prasad Yadav and the party is something BJP will never attain, even if it remains in power for the next five decades. “Do not view this merely as a political statement from him (Tejashwi Yadav). He has worked with Nitish Kumar, and the relationships Nitish ji shares with Lalu ji and our party are such that even if the BJP remains in power for 50 years, it will not have those relationships," he said. He added, "What surprises me is that, in recent years, a stadium has been named after a person while he is still alive, and trains have also been named after him. There was a tradition of waiting until a person passed away, irrespective of whether they held a position or not. Why have we stopped waiting? What does this haste indicate? History will assess it.” His remarks came after Yadav on Saturday criticised the ruling National Democratic Alliance government over its decision to name the newly constructed six-lane Kachi Dargah–Bidupur Ganga bridge ‘Nitish Setu’ after former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, alleging that the move signals the end of the veteran leader's active political relevance. Speaking to ANI, he said, "It is their government; they can name it whatever they please. They may have named it 'Nitish Setu', but in a way, they have also finished off Nitish Kumar. Usually, such names are given—or statues are erected—in memory of those who are no longer with us. Yet, in this case, the naming has been done while he is still alive. It is as if they are sending a message that, politically, Nitish Kumar is already finished." Naming the Kachi Dargah–Bidupur six-lane bridge ‘Nitish Setu’ marks the first time a landmark public infrastructure project in Bihar has been officially named after him, occurring after he stepped down as Chief Minister. bihar_raw_news.title: JDU's Shyam Rajak hits back at opposition to naming new Bihar bridge after Nitish Kumar
bihar_raw_news.content: National JDU’s Shyam Rajak hits back at opposition to naming new Bihar bridge after Nitish Kumar On Nov 15, 2026 Share Patna, Nov 15 (IANS) Janta Dal-United’s national General Secretary Shyam Rajak on Sunday hit back at Rashtriya Janata Dal supremo Lalu Prasad Yadav’s daughter Rohini Acharya over her objection to a bridge being named after former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, invoking the fodder and bitumen scams to target the party leadership. Taking a swipe at Lalu Prasad’s daughter for demanding that the newly constructed six-lane Kacchi Dargah Raghopur-Bidupur Ganga bridge should be named after her father or as the ‘Social Justice Bridge’, Rajak said that if the state were to be named after political figures, it could also be named after scandals associated with their tenure. “According to them, the entire state of Bihar should be renamed Charanagar. There was the fodder scam and the bitumen scam; a state should be named Bitumen Scam State, or another should be named Fodder Scam State,” he said. He alleged that those who were known for corruption had forgotten the condition of Bihar before 2005 and defended Nitish Kumar’s contribution to the state’s development. “If people who were only known for their corruption speak like this, then probably they have forgotten Bihar before 2005. Our leader, respected Nitish Kumar ji, took charge of a dilapidated Bihar and worked to transform it into a developed and respected state,” he said. Rajak maintained that naming the bridge after Nitish Kumar was not merely an honour for the former Chief Minister but also recognition of the state and its people. “This is not about honouring Nitish Kumar; this is about honouring the entire state, and its people. The bridge is a symbol of remembering a person who, irrespective of their caste, creed, background, religion, and gender, took the people towards better conditions. That person is Nitish Kumar,” he added. Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced the newly constructed six-lane bridge would be renamed as ‘Nitish Setu ‘ after the JD-U President, which the family of veteran leader and RJD chief Lalu Prasad Yadav has opposed. In a post on X, Choudhary said Prime Minister Narendra Modi would dedicate the bridge to the nation during his visit to Bihar on November 21. The Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur bridge project, built at a cost of more than Rs 5,000 crore, is a major infrastructure project connecting North and South Bihar. The state government secured a loan of Rs 3,000 crore from the Asian Development Bank, while the remaining Rs 2,000 crore was funded through its own resources. The decision to construct the bridge was taken in 2015, and its foundation stone was laid in 2016. –IANS sud/vd Share Facebook Twitter Google+ ReddIt WhatsApp Pinterest Email

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : Kharna marks the beginning of 36-hour-long fast - Newsonair
bihar_raw_news.content: News On AIR | November 14, 2026 8:02 PM Bihar: Kharna marks the beginning of 36-hour-long fast On the second day of Chhath Mahaparv, devotees across Bihar today performed the Kharna ritual. With this, the 36-hour-long fast without food and water has begun. After observing a day-long fast, devotees performed prayers in the evening and partook of prasad consisting of jaggery kheer, roti and bananas. Traditionally, the prasad is prepared on a clay stove using mango wood as fuel, with holy Ganga water used in its preparation. With the consumption of the Kharna prasad, devotees have now begun their 36-hour-long Nirjala fast, during which they abstain from both food and water. From a nutritional perspective, the traditional ingredients used in Kharna prasad provide energy that helps the body sustain itself during the prolonged fast. Tomorrow morning, women in households will collectively begin preparing the traditional Thekua prasad. In the evening, devotees will offer Arghya to the setting Sun. The festival will conclude on Monday with the offering of Arghya to the rising Sun. Meanwhile, elaborate arrangements have been made at river ghats, ponds and specially created water bodies across the state for devotees to offer prayers to the Sun God. The ghats and surrounding pathways have been beautifully decorated with colourful rangolis and illuminated with lights. The administration has also made extensive arrangements at various locations to ensure the convenience and safety of devotees.

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will participate in the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, today through video conferencing. The programme marks the 151st birth anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. During the programme, the Prime Minister will inaugurate and lay the foundation stones of 246 development projects worth around three thousand crore rupees. These projects aim to strengthen education, healthcare, livelihoods and community infrastructure for tribal communities across the country. Besides, PM Modi will inaugurate 173 projects, including 38 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) for tribal students and 100 Multi-Purpose Centres. These centres come under the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) and will serve as hubs for service delivery and community activities. The Prime Minister will also lay the foundation stones of 19 new Eklavya Model Residential Schools and 12 Tribal Multipurpose Marketing Centres (TMMCs). He will inaugurate various other projects under PM-JANMAN and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA). In addition, he will lay the foundation stones of 42 other projects under PM-JANMAN and DAJGUA. PM Modi will also inaugurate the Tribal Research Institute (TRI) building in Itanagar, Arunachal Pradesh, and the Ropuiliani Tribal Freedom Fighter Museum in Mizoram. These initiatives aim to preserve tribal culture and heritage. The programme will mark the culmination of Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada, being observed across the country from the 1st to the 15th of this month.

national_raw_news.title: Men’s U-19 Asia Cup: India defeat Pakistan to clinch title for ninth time
national_raw_news.content: In Men’s Cricket, India defeated Pakistan by one wicket in a thrilling final to clinch the Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup title in Muscat, Oman, today. Lower-order batters Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva played sensational knocks to help India snatch victory from the jaws of defeat and successfully chase down a challenging target of 338 runs. Needing three runs off the final delivery, Mohit Ulva struck a boundary to seal India’s record-extending ninth title. Mohit remained unbeaten on 49 off just 26 deliveries, while Manal Chauhan contributed a valuable 47 off 32 balls. Skipper Lakshya Raichandani also played a crucial role with a brilliant 80-run knock. Mohit Ulva was named player of the match, while Aaryavir Sehwag was awarded player of the tournament. Earlier, opting to bat first, Pakistan posted 337 for 9 in their allotted 50 overs. Their innings was powered by a century from Usman Khan and half-centuries from Abdul Qadir and Farhan Yousaf. For India, Kavya Patel led India’s bowling attack, claiming four wickets. President Droupadi Murmu congratulated Team India on winning the Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup. In a social media post, the President lauded the young champions for displaying exceptional skill, determination, and composure throughout the closely contested final match. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has also congratulated the young cricketers. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that today is an outstanding day for Indian cricket. He said that their success will inspire several youngsters. Congratulating young cricketers, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said that the determination, firm resolve, and excellent sportsmanship they demonstrated on the pitch were a masterclass in India’s cricketing excellence.
